title: Shumard Oak: Ancient Shumard Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A fast red oak of southern bottomlands. In Nashville, two flank the site of the home where sculptor William Edmondson carved his way into MoMA.
intro: The Shumard oak is a red oak of southern bottomlands and stream banks, and a fast grower, so a big trunk says less about age than it would on a slower oak. The largest we map is in Algonkian Regional Park outside Leesburg, Virginia, about 4.7 metres round and 33.2 metres tall; the county estimates 200 years. In Nashville two Shumard oaks are the only original features left of the home of William Edmondson, who carved limestone in his backyard and in 1937 became the first African American artist given a solo show at MoMA. Across town at Vanderbilt, the one called Big Al turns out to be the smaller of the pair flanking the door of Cole Hall. Kansas City's metro champion grows on a library lawn and went in as nursery stock in 1968. Park Slope's stands on a Brooklyn sidewalk and turns red to orange in autumn.
